tool.name: RADAR-PD Analyze
tool.description: identify and refine phases in neutron or X-ray powder diffraction data
tool.command:

param.name: radiation
param.label: Diffraction source
param.help: Choose this first. It selects the neutron or X-ray candidate catalog and the appropriate pattern treatment.

param.name: instrument_mode
param.label: Pattern geometry
param.help: Auto detect is recommended unless the file metadata are incomplete or ambiguous.
param.option: Auto detect from data and instrument profile

param.name: database_kind
param.label: Library source
param.help: The built-in MP/COD-derived catalog is the normal choice. A custom archive is produced by the RADAR-PD CIF Library Builder.
param.option: Use a custom RADAR-PD CIF library

param.name: database_archive
param.label: Custom library archive
param.help: Select the ZIP produced by RADAR-PD CIF Library Builder. To upload it from your laptop, click the ... button, then New upload and Choose local file.

param.name: source_kind
param.label: Where is the diffraction pattern?
param.help: Choose laptop/Galaxy history to upload a new local file or select an existing dataset. Use an SNS IPTS option to locate reduced data from the mounted IPTS tree.
param.option: Upload from laptop or select Galaxy history
SNS IPTS: locate from NeXus event metadata
SNS IPTS: locate by instrument, IPTS, run, and bank

validator.message: Choose where RADAR-PD should obtain the diffraction pattern.

param.name: diffraction_pattern
param.label: Measured powder diffraction pattern
param.help: To upload from your laptop, click the ... button, then New upload Beta, Upload from Computer, Browse Files, and Start. RADAR-PD accepts .dat, .xye, .gsa, .gss, .gsas, .fxye, and .xrdml files. Galaxy may internally label these files as data, tabular, or xml; that label does not change the file contents.

validator.message: Select a RADAR-PD powder diffraction file ending in .dat, .xye, .gsa, .gss, .gsas, .fxye, or .xrdml, not a result table or configuration artifact.

param.validator: value is not None and value.name.lower().endswith(('.dat', '.xye', '.gsa', '.gss', '.gsas', '.fxye', '.xrdml'))

param.name: kind
param.label: Instrument profile
param.help: Most analyses should use the matching GSAS-II instrument parameter file. The built-in Cu K-alpha profile is for conventional laboratory PXRD only.
param.option: Use a GSAS-II instrument parameter file
Use built-in laboratory Cu K-alpha profile (X-ray only)

validator.message: Choose an uploaded instrument file or the built-in laboratory PXRD profile.

param.name: instrument_file
param.label: GSAS-II instrument parameter file
param.help: Select the matching profile. To upload from your laptop, click the ... button, then New upload Beta, Upload from Computer, Browse Files, and Start. RADAR-PD accepts .instprm, .prm, .inst, and .ins profiles even when Galaxy labels them as generic data.

validator.message: Select a GSAS-II instrument parameter file ending in .instprm, .prm, .inst, or .ins, not a report or configuration artifact.

param.validator: value is not None and value.name.lower().endswith(('.instprm', '.prm', '.inst', '.ins'))

param.name: event_file
param.label: NeXus event file
param.help: RADAR-PD uses its instrument, IPTS, and run metadata to locate one reduced powder pattern and matching instrument profile.

param.name: bank
param.label: Reduced-data bank override
param.help: Required only when more than one matching reduced bank exists.

param.name: instrument
param.label: Instrument
param.help: For example HB2A.

param.name: ipts
param.label: IPTS
param.help: For example IPTS-32001.

param.name: main_cif
param.label: Known/main phase CIF
param.help: Supply a .cif file when the dominant structural phase is known. To upload from your laptop, click the ... button, then New upload Beta, Upload from Computer, Browse Files, and Start. RADAR-PD anchors and protects this phase before searching its residual signal.

validator.message: Select a crystallographic information file ending in .cif.

param.name: sample_elements
param.label: Elements expected in the sample
param.help: Comma- or space-separated symbols, for example Cu, P, Pb, O, S. Leave out sample-can elements unless they are chemically part of the specimen.

validator.message: Enter at least one sample element.

param.name: environment_elements
param.label: Sample can / environment elements
param.help: These may appear as pure environment phases but are not freely combined with the sample chemistry. Examples include Al or V.

param.name: limit_start
param.label: Fit range start
param.help: Native x-axis units: degrees 2-theta for CW/PXRD or microseconds for TOF.

param.name: limit_end
param.label: Fit range end
param.help: Both fit-range values must be supplied together.

repeat.name: excluded_regions
repeat.title: Ignored region
repeat.help: Exclude known artifacts or unreliable intervals from refinement and residual analysis.

param.name: presets
param.label: Structures to mask
param.help: RADAR-PD calculates Bragg positions and creates instrument-aware ignored windows. This is separate from the environment-element chemistry policy.

param.name: include_kbeta
param.label: Also mask Cu K-beta companion positions
param.help: Relevant to Cu-anode laboratory PXRD.

param.name: background_mode
param.label: Correction strategy
param.help: Automatic fixed points is the scale-aware default used to seed GSAS-II background refinement.

param.name: enabled
param.label: Run commensurate magnetic peak precheck
param.help: Use only for neutron data with a supplied main CIF. It tests whether residual peaks are systematically indexed by a propagation vector; it does not solve a magnetic structure.
param.option: Yes, inspect residual peaks before phase search

param.name: denominators
param.label: Commensurate denominators
param.help: Comma-separated positive integers, normally 2,3.

param.name: main_prenudge
param.label: Automatically anchor a supplied main-phase cell
param.help: A guarded pre-nudge is triggered only when the starting main CIF does not adequately align with the measured peaks.

param.name: main_shadow_filter
param.label: Filter candidates supported only by strong main-phase peaks
param.help: The filter fails open when the main-phase anchor is not reliable, preventing accidental removal of all hypotheses.

param.name: main_cleanup
param.label: Refine supplied main-CIF internal parameters after lattice anchoring

param.name: analysis_mode
param.label: Analysis path
param.help: All measurement, library, data, chemistry, masking, background, magnetic, and main-phase settings above are shared by both routes. Only the search strategy below changes.

param.name: profile_kind
param.label: Full RADAR-PD search profile
param.help: Balanced is recommended for a first scientific run. Quick is diagnostic; Thorough broadens the sequential residual search when unexplained peaks remain.

param.name: nudge_candidates
param.label: Candidates sent to lattice nudging per round

param.name: compare_candidates
param.label: Candidates compared in each commit cycle

param.name: rwp_improvement_threshold
param.label: Stop when Rwp improvement falls below

param.name: phases_per_hypothesis
param.label: Candidate phases in each hypothesis
param.help: With a supplied main CIF, this is the maximum number of impurity candidates. Without a main CIF, it is the total number of phases in a hypothesis.

param.name: stage_output_limit
param.label: Hypotheses retained for inspection
param.help: Controls how many ranked combinations remain visible at each Rapid stage; it does not alter diffraction physics.

param.name: gsas_validation_limit
param.label: Final refinement checks
param.help: Number of shortlisted hypotheses sent to guarded GSAS-II refinement. Zero stops after lattice-aware pattern scoring.

param.name: parallel_workers
param.label: Parallel refinement workers
param.help: Independent final hypotheses are refined in parallel. Four is the production default.

param.name: family_variants
param.label: Keep alternate members of near-stoichiometric phase families
param.help: Preserves scientifically comparable CIF variants for later inspection while ranking one preferred representative.

param.name: final_polish
param.label: Run deeper final cell polish
param.help: Normally leave off. Enable only when the focused final refinement requires an additional guarded cell-polish stage.

param.name: run_name
param.label: Run name
param.help: Defaults to the diffraction dataset name. Use a meaningful name for mapped scans or repeated measurements.

param.name: config_kind
param.label: Configuration source
param.help: Most users should generate the configuration from the controls above. A saved YAML is useful in automated or mapped workflows.
param.option: Generate a reproducible configuration from this form
Use a saved RADAR-PD YAML configuration

param.name: config_file
param.label: Saved RADAR-PD configuration
param.help: Scientific settings above are replaced by this YAML; input datasets, candidate library, and run name are still selected here.

collection.name: phases
collection.label: RADAR-PD 5 | Candidate and refined phase CIFs

tool.help:
**RADAR-PD analysis workflow**
1. Choose neutron or X-ray diffraction, then provide the common scientific inputs in Sections 2-8. 2. Select the built-in catalog or a custom CIF library built with the companion Library Builder. 3. Supply data directly from Galaxy history or resolve a reduced SNS IPTS run. Add a main-phase CIF when the dominant structure is known. 4. Enter sample chemistry separately from sample-can or environment elements. 5. Review optional pattern masks, background treatment, magnetic precheck, and known-main-phase safeguards. 6. In Section 9, choose Full RADAR-PD or Rapid Hypothesis Mode. Switching routes changes only the execution controls in that section; it does not replace or hide the scientific inputs above.
**Rapid Hypothesis Mode** performs coarse mixture search, symmetry-aware lattice nudging, higher-resolution pattern scoring, and focused GSAS-II refinement ranking. **Full RADAR-PD** performs sequential residual-aware impurity discovery and refinement. The Balanced profile is recommended for a first Full run.
The primary outputs are numbered in the History. Open **Results dashboard** with the companion **RADAR-PD Utility: Explore Results** tool for an integrated view of hypotheses, fit plots, timings, phase fractions, warnings, downloads, and GPX checkpoints. Use **GSAS-II Project Handoff** to continue a selected refinement in the hosted GSAS-II interface.
